lesson.child_mission: The places unit review links the features of a place, natural and built features, map skills, Australia's states and capitals, world locations, comparing places and the causes of similarity and difference.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Match each part of the showcase to the skill it shows: key and compass; table; comparison; cause.

FEEDBACK
Key and compass: map reading; table: sorting features; comparison: using criteria; cause: geographic reasoning.

WATCH FOR
A poster of pretty pictures with no key, criteria or sources shows decoration rather than geographic thinking.

INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Assemble a places showcase using the checklist, practise a one-minute talk and write two questions for another place study.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.

Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Assemble a places showcase using the checklist, practise a one-minute talk and write two questions for another place study. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Likely misconception: A poster of pretty pictures with no key, criteria or sources shows decoration rather than geographic thinking. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating review on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with review, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

teach_steps.explain:
The places unit review links the features of a place, natural and built features, map skills, Australia's states and capitals, world locations, comparing places and the causes of similarity and difference.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner base claims on sources, places and respectful community knowledge, rather than guessing from a single picture. Keep every claim linked to evidence.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the sources, map features or community examples that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Compare your record with the feedback: did you use the same skill and show your evidence? If a detail is uncertain, identify what source you would need next. One deliberate, evidence-based revision is more useful than writing a longer answer.
